title: Retreat order replaces the free Call it off
overseerSummary: Before contact, Call it off works as today. After contact the button becomes Order a retreat: the squad walks to extraction and the contract ends as a loss through the normal settlement, deaths included. Measured on combat.js: 8.2% of won sorties have a death.

proposals.title: After first contact, replace the free 'Call it off' with a retreat order that ends the contract as a loss
proposals.problem: abandon() frees the whole party and Roster.fall only runs at settlement, so a squad member who fell on the map is alive again after one click. Measured on combat.js (not the attrition resolver): 147 of 900 sorties had a death, 52 of 631 won sorties (8.2%) had at least one, and 268 deaths in total, 67 of them in won sorties. A player who presses 'Call it off' at the first fall keeps all of those people and forgoes 8.2% of wins (counted by sortie, not payout-weighted). Every death-prevention feature (wormhole escape hatch, break-off, potions, tactics retreat) and every death-consequence system (grief, memorial, bonds 'survived', Crew.mourn) is worth little while this free undo exists.
evidence: sortie.js:338-350 abandon() clears c.mission for all party members, forget(), run = null; no alive check, no Roster.fall, no Condition or Bonds call
sortie.js:450 Roster.fall is only reached from settle() (sortie.js:439), which tick() calls only when s.result is set
sortie.js:1269, 1275, 1335-1337 the button stays visible until s.result exists, i.e. through the whole walk home
sortie.js:1387 window.Sortie already exports abandon, so keeping it exported costs nothing and covers console/dev use
sortie.js:983 UI text says 'Leaving the page abandons a run in progress'; persist/resume (sortie.js:299-336) keeps the run, so the text is false

field.js:1217-1231 openSkirmish resolves the whole fight when it opens; field.js:1235-1248 plays it back and deaths land at kill() (field.js:1251) when playback ends. An order cannot save anyone already in an open fight.

field.js:382-397 withdraw()/pullOut(); field.js:1350-1360 portalTick treats s.withdrew as work done so the way home forms; field.js:72 STRAGGLE = 900 in-game s; field.js:1600-1607 verdict() ends a withdrawn run as a loss, 'could not get clear' after STRAGGLE

field.js:877 counters.spotted++ when a hostile sees the squad; field.js:2052 counters initialised; field.js:1977 and 2015 counters are saved and restored, so contact derived from counters survives a reload

field.js:1318-1326 workDone() returns true immediately for escort (only fetch-type atoms count), so a workDone guard would refuse every escort retreat; found by test (refuse.js, 16 types x 10 seeds), replaced by a predicate over win atoms
field.js:1458-1462 callBack() is the existing player-to-field order; field.js:2139-2141 FieldAPI exports callBack and not withdraw

MEASURED, combat.js-backed runner at C:\Users\mersi\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-mersi-Documents-InfiniteGacha\bdec2eb2-03df-4be6-b387-8df61798b109\scratchpad\loop2\real.js (mirrors sortie.js resolve() and the REGEN tick; 15 contract types x 60 seeds = 900 sorties; 4 random 3-5 star characters with eligible classes, no gear or potions; contract level 1-4; tactics on): baseline win 70.1%, 0.298 deaths per sortie, 16.3% of sorties with a death

MEASURED, same runner, contract level matched to roster stars (no retreat): 1-2 stars level<=2: win 37%, 0.53 deaths/sortie, 25% with a death; 2-3 stars level<=3: 49%, 0.47, 23%; 4-5 stars level<=5: 71%, 0.26, 15%. No gear or potions in the runner, so these are upper bounds for a real roster.

MEASURED, free window: first hostile sighting of the squad at median 75 in-game s (p10 28, p90 186); first fight opens at median 82 (p10 34, p90 184). At 1x (5 in-game s per real s) the free 'Call it off' lasts about 15 real s (p10 6 s, p90 37 s).

MEASURED, retreat ordered at the first calm moment after contact (821 of 900 sorties accepted it; 60 were escorts, which are 'homeward' by definition): all 821 ended through verdict; 0 reached STRAGGLE; time from order to result p50 60 in-game s, p90 105, max 290 of 900. Gate n=380 p50 81 max 270; window n=298 p50 53 max 290; standfast n=143 p50 2 max 42. On the largest maps (area >= 70% of the largest generated, n=320) max 290, 0 stragglers. Deaths after the order: 13 across 821 sorties.

MEASURED, retreat as a survival tool: ordered between fights when average squad HP < 70%: 67 orders, win 65.3% (baseline 70.1%), 0.287 deaths/sortie (0.298). HP < 50%: 12 orders, no change. After first fall: 8 orders, no change. In 109 of the 147 sorties with a death the squad had already withdrawn on its own; median time from first fall to the end of the sortie is 62 in-game s.

MEASURED, save/restore: scratchpad\loop2\roundtrip.js, 46 contacted runs across 6 contract types: contacted() true after save -> JSON -> restore in 46/46; withdrew and phase survive; all 46 ended through verdict
proposals.change:
1. field.js, beside callBack (field.js:1458), four small functions over state that is already saved:
   const contacted = (s) => (s.counters.fights || 0) > 0 || (s.counters.spotted || 0) > 0;   // openSkirmish adds s.counters.fights++ (field.js:1217)
   const homeward = (s) => s.mission.win.every(a => a.atom === 'extract' || winMet(s, a));   // every term met except getting out
   function exitState(s) { if (s.result) return 'over'; if (s.withdrew) return 'retreating'; if (s.escalated) return 'escaping'; if (!contacted(s)) return 'free'; return homeward(s) ? 'homeward' : 'order'; }
   function retreat(s) { if (exitState(s) !== 'order') return false; withdraw(s, 'called back'); return true; }
   Export exitState, retreat, contacted in FieldAPI (field.js:2139-2141). Older saves have no counters.fights and read as 0.
2. sortie.js: the exit button (sortie.js:1269, 1275, 1335) reads F.exitState(run.field) on every renderSide(): 'free' = 'Call it off' (abandon(), unchanged); 'order' = 'Order a retreat' (F.retreat(run.field)); 'retreating' = 'Retreating' (disabled); 'escaping' = 'Escaping' (disabled); 'homeward' = 'Heading home' (disabled). One line under the button states the rule for the current state: free = 'Free until the squad is seen or a fight opens'; order = 'Ends the contract as a loss; takes effect when the current fight ends'.
3. settle() needs no change. Falls, grief, bonds 'survived', Crew.completed, trial failure (Quests.fail, sortie.js:527-530), Condition.outcome and salvage loot already run for a lost result. The result line reads 'called back' or 'called back, and could not get clear'.
4. Replace the sentence at sortie.js:983 with: 'A run in progress is saved and resumes after a reload. Call it off is free until the squad is seen or a fight opens; after that the squad can be ordered out, which ends the contract as a loss.'
5. No standfast hold: a standfast retreat completes in about 2 in-game s because the door opens where the squad stands (field.js:1381-1389). Escort has no retreat state after contact: its win atoms are all extractions, so the walk out is the contract and exitState reports 'homeward'.
6. Build as one unit with loop-wounds, the live squad list from loop-readout, and the per-type record plus fall cause from loop-ledger part A. Without those the player loses the free undo and gains no information to replace it.
7. Test to add to test/: exitState/retreat across portal modes (gate, window, standfast), save/restore round trip, and every contract type reaching a result within STRAGGLE after a retreat order. scratchpad\loop2\real.js is the prototype of a combat.js-backed harness and can be moved into test/.
proposals.playerEffect: Launching a squad becomes a commitment once the squad is seen or a fight opens. The decisions that remain are made before launch: which contract type (measured deaths per sortie range from 0.01 for escort to 1.26 for assassination, see loop-ledger), who goes, and what they carry. During a watch the player can still give up a hopeless contract, and the squad walks out on a path that has been measured to terminate, but the data says the order rarely saves a life: it works between fights, and in combat.js most deaths are in the fight that decides the sortie. The retreat is therefore a bail-out that costs the contract, not a lifesaver, and the proposal should be described that way.
proposals.secondOrder: Escape features gain value: the Chorokinetic wormhole and breakOff (field.js:989-1050), healing potions supplied by Outfit (outfit.js:27-33, 150-167), tactics 'a step back'. Grief, the memorial, team rapport loss (Crew.mourn) and the bonds 'survived' event occur at the rate the sim produces them instead of near zero for an attentive player. Skip becomes an explicit acceptance of risk. A trial that ends in a retreat re-rolls through the existing Quests.fail path, and the trial fee is already spent (quests.js:165-175), so a trial retreat costs the fee plus the re-roll. Wounds (loop-wounds) become the non-fatal outcome for survivors. Contract-type choice becomes the main survival lever, which is why the per-type record ships in the same build.
proposals.risks: Deaths per sortie for an attentive player rise from near zero to the simulated rate: 0.26 deaths per sortie at 4-5 stars, 0.30 at 3-5 stars, 0.47-0.53 at 1-3 stars with matched contract levels (upper bounds: the runner has no gear or potions). That is a large difficulty change for the early game and will read as a nerf; the mitigation is information (loop-ledger per-type record, loop-readout) and wounds, not the retreat order. Free window is short (about 15 real seconds at 1x) because a hostile sighting usually precedes the first fight by under 10 s; if that is too short, define contact as fights > 0 only (window medians are within 7 in-game s, so the choice barely moves it). A 'quiet' side job resets counters.spotted (field.js:468), which can reopen the free window if no fight has happened yet; acceptable, and a latch would add a saved field. Hiding the tab flushes the open fight (Field.save calls flushSkirmishes, field.js:1971-1972; sortie.js:1402 persist(true) on visibilitychange), so tabbing away after an order ends the current fight at once; behaviour exists today and needs a note, not a change. Browser check by the overseer: the five button states, and that they survive a reload. All figures are from the plain-character combat.js runner and need a confirming sample on a real save.
proposals.response: Design attack (the order cannot change the fight being watched; the lever is pre-contact): accepted and stated in the proposal; the order is described as a bail-out and the measured data supports the attack (hp<70% policy: -0.011 deaths per sortie, -5 points of wins). Free abandon is kept before contact exactly as today, with the window measured (about 15 real seconds). Design attack (removes the only exit from a stalled run): every post-contact state has a bound in verdict(); 821 retreat orders ended in a result with max 290 of 900 STRAGGLE seconds across gate, window and standfast, including the largest maps; Sortie.abandon stays exported. Design demand (ships with the live HP block): accepted, moved into loop-readout as a per-member list that does not spoil an open fight. Design demand (button state survives reload): the state is derived from saved fields (counters, withdrew, escalated, phase), round trip tested 46/46 in Node; the browser check is left to the overseer. Design demand (largest three maps): measured in Node with the real field.js and mapgen, 320 sorties on maps >= 70% of the largest area, 0 stragglers. Engineering demand 1 (abandon reachable as a backstop; retreat refuses only when withdrawn): abandon stays exported and is the pre-contact control; retreat also refuses 'escaping', 'homeward' and 'over' because ordering in those states changes nothing. Engineering demand 2 (Node test across portal modes): done for the prototype, specified as a test/ file. Engineering demand 3 (same build as loop-wounds): accepted, together with the roster list and per-type record. Engineering demand 4 (tab-hide flush note): verified at field.js:1971-1972 and sortie.js:1402, recorded in risks. Engineering demand 5 (button state survives reload): see above. One change forced by checking: the original guard on workDone() refuses every escort retreat (workDone is true at tick 1 for escort), so it was replaced by the homeward predicate.

verdicts.attack: The order cannot change the fight the player is watching: combat.js resolves the whole skirmish when it opens (field.js:1217-1225) and deaths land when the playback ends (field.js:1242), so after the first '⚔️ meet' line the button only decides whether the squad walks out before the NEXT group arrives. The real lever is pre-contact, where 'Call it off' already exists and stays free. After contact the proposal also removes the only exit from a stalled run until STRAGGLE (900 in-game s, field.js:1606) ends it. A retreat-every-time player loses only the contract and a trial reroll, but that is the intended price and it already costs more than abandon does today (Condition.outcome -12 at condition.js:196, Quests.fail at sortie.js:528), so this is not a disguised nerf.
verdicts.evidenceCheck: Verified: abandon() sortie.js:338-350 clears c.mission with no alive check and no Roster.fall; Roster.fall only at sortie.js:450 inside settle(), reached only when s.result is set (sortie.js:387); kill() marks the actor only (field.js:1251-1268); withdraw/pullOut field.js:382-397; portalTick treats s.withdrew as done (field.js:1355); verdict ends a withdrawn run (field.js:1600-1607); FieldAPI exports callBack and not withdraw (field.js:2139-2141); persist/resume keep a run across reloads so only the button undoes a death. My harness run at POW 0.6 (420 runs) reproduces 77% wins and 0.28-0.30 deaths/run. The '6% of payouts' figure is from the plain attrition resolver and is relative only.
verdicts.demand: Keep 'Call it off' before contact exactly as today. After contact the retreat must end through settle() as a loss with no new settlement path. Ship the live standing/total and average-HP block from loop-readout in the same change, or the order is a blind guess. Confirm s.withdrew and s.phase survive Field.save/restore (field.js:1975-2025) so the button state is right after a reload. Verify in the browser, not the harness, that a squad under retreat on a gate contract actually reaches the portal within STRAGGLE on the three largest maps.

verdicts.attack: After first contact the player loses the only recovery from a run whose verdict never arrives; the order cannot save anyone inside an open skirmish because openSkirmish (field.js:1217-1225) receives the whole fight already resolved and kill() lands deaths at playback end (field.js:1251-1262); the death rate for an attentive player goes from ~0 to the simulated rate (my stock harness at POW 0.6, 6 runs/type: 0.34 dead/run, 27% withdrew), which reads as a nerf unless wounds ship with it; on standfast contracts portalTick opens the door where the squad stands (field.js:1381-1389) so a retreat there costs only the contract.
verdicts.evidenceCheck: Verified sortie.js:338-350 abandon() clears c.mission for the party, calls forget(), no alive check, no Roster.fall; Roster.fall only at sortie.js:450 inside settle(); #sortie-abandon stays until s.result (sortie.js:1269, 1335-1337); withdraw/pullOut at field.js:382-397; taskGoal returns exit when s.withdrew; portalTick treats withdrew as done; verdict returns a loss with 'could not get clear' after STRAGGLE 900; FieldAPI (field.js:2139-2141) exports callBack and not withdraw; 'found' and 'spotted' are in ACTOR_KEYS (field.js:1939-1943). Ran the builder's retreat.harness.js at POW 0.6 x6: 13.9% runs with a death, 2.8% won with a death, structurally matching the cited 14.3%/5.7.
verdicts.demand: 1) Keep Sortie.abandon reachable as a backstop (console export or after STRAGGLE) and have retreat() refuse only when s.withdrew is already set. 2) Add 'retreat' to FieldAPI with a Node test that a contacted run terminates through verdict within STRAGGLE for gate, window and standfast portal modes. 3) Ship in the same build as loop-wounds so a watched run has an outcome between fine and dead. 4) Note beside the button that persist(true) on tab-hide flushes the open fight (field.js:1971-1972, sortie.js:1402), so tabbing away after the order resolves the fight at once. 5) Overseer confirms in the browser that the three button states survive a reload (resume rebuilds from s.withdrew).
